cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: For Stability’s Sake
cards.instruction: Hide a destabilizing truth because you believe the current balance of power must be protected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Keep the treasurer's page out of the fair briefing. Our chair needs everyone's confidence today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She spent the stall money on that arch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Call it donated decoration. If the stallholders find out, they'll replace her before we open.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cover the shortfall, but she must sign an IOU.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Privately, after her welcome. Let them see her opening the fair, not borrowing to open it.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 commands omission, A3 dictates a false donation account and A5 permits the rescue only privately after the welcome, making superior control protect existing leadership.

heightening.evidence: B4 helpful IOU solution becomes A5 another managed visibility issue, preserving the public welcome before private borrowing.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 opening rather than borrowing to open earns its contrast from B4 actual loan, not a new obstacle.
